sections.heading: License responsibilities, points and sanctions
sections.markdown:
## C — License responsibilities, points and sanctions

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A25
A person cannot simultaneously hold a Nebraska driving permit or license and a state identification card. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A25
A document issued on lawful-status evidence is valid only for the authorized U.S. stay, or for a year when that stay has no definite end. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A25
Nebraska will not issue a license while driving privileges are suspended or revoked in any state or jurisdiction. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A25
Suspension temporarily removes a person’s valid license and driving privilege. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A25
Revocation removes the driving privilege and takes the license for a specified period. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A25
A suspension or revocation continues until the driver satisfies reinstatement requirements and pays required fees. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A25
Impoundment means a court holds the license and prohibits driving for the ordered period. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A25
Confiscation means an officer seizes the license after an alcohol-test failure or refusal. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A25
After confiscation, the issued temporary license lasts 15 days. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A25
At the end of that temporary-license period, revocation follows unless a departmental hearing dismisses the violation. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A25
A motor-vehicle homicide can cause loss of a license. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A25
Repeated traffic violations in any state can cause loss of driving privileges. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A25
Using a vehicle to commit a crime can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A25
A drug- or alcohol-impaired-driving arrest or conviction can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A25
Falsifying or concealing application information can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A25
Leaving a crash without providing a name and address can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A25
Ignoring a citation or court judgment in Nebraska or another state can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A25
Alcoholism or drug addiction can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A25
Flight from an officer to avoid arrest can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A25
Refusing a chemical test can lead to license loss. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A25
Reckless driving can lead to loss of the license. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A26
Lending a driver license to another person can lead to license loss. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A26
Having another person take the licensing test can lead to license loss. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A26
A conviction for failing to show insurance proof can lead to license loss. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A26
Failure to comply with a child-support or alimony order can lead to license loss. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A26
A driver younger than 21 can lose driving privileges for failing to complete required improvement training after accumulating 6 points in a year. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A26
Transporting a child while intoxicated can lead to license loss. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A26
Violating school learner, school or learner permit terms also bars eligibility for another permit until age 16. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A26
Accumulating 12 points within 2 years automatically revokes the operator license for 6 months. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A26
The DMV’s point-revocation letter directs the driver to surrender the license. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A26
Failure to surrender the revoked license can bring a fine up to 500 dollars, up to 30 days in county jail, or both. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A26
Point-based reinstatement requires a DMV-approved driver-education course of at least 4 hours at the driver’s expense. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A26
After point revocation, financial-responsibility proof must remain in force for 3 years after the original revocation ends. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A26
A second Nebraska point revocation within 5 years removes driving privileges for 3 years. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A26
A motor-vehicle-homicide conviction carries 12 points. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A26
A third drunk-driving offense carries 12 points. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A26
Failure to report a crash to law enforcement carries 6 points. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A26
Failure to help after a crash involving the driver carries 6 points. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A27
Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs carries 6 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A27
Willful reckless driving carries 6 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F41 | anchor: A27
Leaving a crash scene carries 6 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F42 | anchor: A27
Reckless driving carries 5 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F43 | anchor: A27
Careless driving carries 4 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F44 | anchor: A27
Failure to yield that injures a pedestrian carries 4 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F45 | anchor: A27
Using a handheld wireless device to read, type or send written messages while driving carries 3 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F46 | anchor: A27
Negligent driving carries 3 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F47 | anchor: A27
Passing a school bus with its stop arm out and red lights flashing carries 3 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F48 | anchor: A27
Failure to yield to a pedestrian without injury carries 2 points. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F49 | anchor: A27
Unlawfully blocking the driver’s view carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F50 | anchor: A27
Refusal of an alcohol-content test carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F51 | anchor: A27
A child-restraint violation carries one point. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> pdf-0027]

Misconceptions: The end of a stated suspension period does not itself complete reinstatement.
Mnemonics: Temporary loss still needs reinstatement; special permits allow only their stated trips.
Glossary: Suspension temporarily removes driving privileges; revocation removes privileges for a specified period; impoundment is court retention; confiscation is officer seizure.
Dynamic facts: Changing contacts, officials, live services and fees are withheld from the stable rule inventory.
